people.role: Valley-mistress of Thải Chi Cốc since 1000: the herb terraces, the pills, and the river's orphans
people.appearance: A square, sun-browned woman in a field apron, with soil under her nails and a gourd at her hip that smells of every herb at once.
people.backstory: Nghiêm Linh Chi was four when a spring flood took Hà Đê Thôn's dike and her parents with it in 924. A herb-picker of the valley, Cố Hoài Sơn (co_hoai_son), found her on a roof and carried her up the river in a basket. She grew up weeding his terraces and tasted the hundred herbs at sixty. When he died in his field in 1000 she became valley-mistress, and in her first spring she opened the herb fields to the river's orphans (A078). They have come ever since: flood children, ferry children, the children of the Ferry War. She names them after herbs and gives them her own surname. She sells the pines' Pill Room what Bồ Hạnh Lâm (bo_hanh_lam), whom the valley sent there at nine, cannot brew. The River Hall's mistress Dụ Tĩnh Lưu (du_tinh_luu) sends her grain for the children. She has kept the valley out of every war for two hundred years by being needed by both sides. In the winter of 1174 she treated Lạc Hà's wounded raiders from the Đào Sa burning in the lower field and sent them home, and the whole river knows it: Giang Cửu Khúc (giang_cuu_khuc) buys her pills anyway, and his ferrymen spit on her landing.
people.wants: To keep every child carried up the river, and to bring Lữ Niệm Hà's brother home from Lạc Hà before one of them dies.
people.secret: Since 1176 the River Hall's grain has been paid for with the oldest orphans' days on its dikes, and the valley keeps the wages left over. She read the first contract, in the autumn the grain ran short, and she has sealed every one since on the landing without opening it.

people.role: Guest elder and the valley's furnace-master; the last alchemist of Lăng Tiêu Các
people.exception: guest elder (khách khanh): a hired alchemist with a Fire root, never taught the valley's canon
people.appearance: A gaunt man with burn-scarred forearms who keeps a bronze censer with a live coal in it on a chain at his belt.
people.backstory: He was the youngest master of the pill hall of Lăng Tiêu Các on its mountain when the hall burned in 1066 and its alchemists scattered (V050). He walked down to the valley with the Cinder Censer and nothing else, and Nghiêm Linh Chi (nghiem_linh_chi) gave him a stone furnace-house below the terraces, where open fire cannot reach the herbs. He brews what the Wood canon cannot. He has never said whose furnace the fire started in. The scattered alchemists of Lăng Tiêu still ask after him.
people.wants: To learn whether anyone of Lăng Tiêu still lives who remembers whose furnace it was, before they come looking for him.
people.secret: He is copying the pill hall's forbidden recipes onto Phùng Lục Ngạc's (phung_luc_ngac) practice sheets, a page a night, so something of Lăng Tiêu outlives him; he tells her they are exercises.

people.role: The mistress's true disciple; a ferryman's daughter of Đào Sa, orphaned in the Ferry War
people.appearance: A wiry woman with a ferryman's hands, who keeps a burnt nail from the Đào Sa landing on a string round her neck.
people.backstory: She was ten when Lạc Hà's raiders burned Lãng Đào's boats at the Đào Sa landing (A080) with her father Lữ Thừa Lãng (lu_thua_lang) on one of them. A Lạc Hà elder took her little brother Lữ Tẫn Chu (lu_tan_chu) home across the border; she was sent up the river to the valley with the other ferry orphans. She refused an herb name and kept her own. Nghiêm Linh Chi (nghiem_linh_chi) made her a true disciple at thirty. She keeps the long houses, and each flood season she picks the names for the River Hall's dike crews, oldest first, and walks them down to the river herself. She has written to her brother every year. He sings for the side that burned their father, and he has never answered.
people.wants: To walk her brother out of Lạc Hà and onto the valley's landing, and never again to put a child under fifteen on the dike list.
people.secret: She is buying the oldest orphans' dike days back from Ông Khổ Sâm (ong_kho_sam) one name at a time out of her own pill-sale stipend, and has bought nine; Ông has noticed the coin and priced the days up.

people.role: Field-warden of the herb terraces; holds the Grain Rain canon after the mistress
people.appearance: A bent old farmer with a hoe he will not let anyone else carry and a knee that tells him the rain.
people.backstory: A herb-gatherer's son from Bối Dược Thôn, he has kept the terraces since 1080 and called the Grain Rain over the drowned river fields in the flood of 1093, when Khang Tẩy Kim's gold-washers were pulled from the water downstream. He is 160 and will not form a Golden Core. Every flood season since 1176 Lữ Niệm Hà (lu_niem_ha) has taken his best weeders down to the River Hall's dikes, and he works the terraces with the under-tens and says so at every meal. He has not said it to Nghiêm Linh Chi (nghiem_linh_chi).
people.wants: To keep the terraces tended by weeders of fifteen and over, and to die in his own field with a seed of his herb in each hand.
people.secret: Each flood season he hides six of his best weeders in the disused drying-shed on dike-list mornings and has them written down as sick; Nghiêm Kim Ngân (nghiem_kim_ngan) signs the sick-roll and asks no questions.

people.backstory: A Mạch Hương Thôn girl with a little Fire in her root, which the valley's canon has no use for and Diêu Tẫn Đan (dieu_tan_dan) does; she spends her nights in his stone furnace-house. A coin she never shows decides which outer child gets the pill-ends she sweeps from the floor, and Nghiêm Bạc Hà (nghiem_bac_ha) has not won one in a year.

people.role: Founder of Thải Chi Cốc (480); one of the lingzhi pickers who left the world
people.backstory: One of the four pickers who walked into the valley in 480 singing the old song of the four hermits (A071). She grew the gourd on her own vine, planted the first spirit-herb fields along the river in 520 (A072), and taught the valley to sing its canon instead of writing it. She died sitting under a lingzhi in 690, the same year the pines' founder died (A010).
